newsitem.title: ITALY: Any euro doubts now gone, Italy in at start - Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Any euro doubts now gone, Italy in at start - Ciampi.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Wednesday that any lingering doubts about whether Europe's planned single currency, the euro, would be launched on time in 1999 had now been removed.
Ciampi, addressing the Italian banking association ABI, also said that Italy would be a member of economic and monetary union from the start.
"Any residual doubt that the euro will start on time has been resolved," Ciampi said.
"Italy will be able to participate from the start."
Confidence about Italy's chances of becoming a founder member of the single currency has gathered momentum in recent days, propelling stock indices and debt markets to record highs.

Italy, once considered a euro no-hoper, was congratulated by Brussels on Tuesday and Europe's fledgling central bank put the icing on the cake by issuing a bond priced in lira which can be redenominated into euros once the new currency is launched -- showing that it also believes Italy could make the grade.
